fixes.explanation: Bethsaida it is, friend. Luke says Jesus took the apostles away privately and withdrew to a town called Bethsaida (Luke 9:10). The apostles are the Twelve, the men Jesus sent out earlier (Luke 6:13; 9:1–2). Just a quiet getaway with His closest followers, and you know how well quiet worked out.

Capernaum is a town Jesus visits in Luke 4:31, so I see why it came to mind. But Luke 9:10 names a different place: Bethsaida. That's where Jesus withdrew with the apostles. Pack your bags for Bethsaida this time, friend, not Capernaum.

Nazareth is where Jesus was brought up (Luke 4:16), but it isn't the town here. Luke says Jesus took the apostles away privately to a town called Bethsaida (Luke 9:10). I've mixed up my own cookie trays plenty of times, so no shame here. Bethsaida is the one to remember.

Not quite, friend. The text says the opposite: the crowds found out and followed Him, and He welcomed them (Luke 9:11). He had withdrawn privately (Luke 9:10), and I think that makes the welcome worth a pause.
False is right! Luke 9:11 says that He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God. No sending anybody away, no sign on the door. A crowd follows Him and He makes room for them anyway.

Heals, yes! The text says He healed those who needed healing (Luke 9:11). So the crowd got teaching about the kingdom of God and healing from Him. That's a lot of work, and the Twelve haven't even brought up food yet.

Anointing shows up in Luke too (Luke 7:46), but it's not what Luke 9:11 says here. The verse says Jesus healed those who needed healing. So the word that fits the blank is heals. Good guess on a Bible word, though, friend.

Baptizing shows up in Luke (Luke 3:16), but not in this verse. Luke 9:11 says Jesus welcomed the crowds, spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and healed those who needed healing. So the blank wants heals. Easy one to mix up when so many Bible words are floating around.

The text doesn't say anything about teaching through the night. As the day neared its end, the Twelve asked Jesus to "Dismiss the crowd…" so people could find lodging and provisions (Luke 9:12). Jesus had been teaching and healing the crowd (Luke 9:11), so I think that sounds like a long shift already.

Five loaves and two fish, right on the money. The disciples answered, "We have only five loaves of bread and two fish…" (Luke 9:13). That was their answer to "You give them something to eat." I've seen a bigger stash in my cookie jar on a slow Tuesday.

Close in spirit, but the numbers don't match. The disciples said, "We have only five loaves of bread and two fish…" (Luke 9:13). Seven loaves shows up in a different story (Mark 8:5), so I see how it slipped in. For this one, hold on to five loaves and two fish.

You've got the right numbers, just swapped, friend! It's five loaves and two fish, as the disciples said in Luke 9:13. I do that with my own recipes, and my cookies come out strange. Flip those numbers and you've got it.

Standing in lines isn't what Jesus asked for. He said, "Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each." (Luke 9:14) So it's sitting, in groups, and about fifty. A hundred is a nice round number, but it isn't the one in the verse.

The Twelve did ask Jesus to dismiss the crowd so they could go to the surrounding villages and countryside (Luke 9:12). But Jesus gave a different instruction: "Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each." (Luke 9:14) So the instruction is to sit down.

HEAVEN is right! Luke 9:16 says Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, spoke a blessing and broke them. Look up, bless, break. Three moves, and that's the order Luke gives them.
Satisfied, yes! Luke 9:17 says, "They all ate and were satisfied…" Five loaves and two fish, about five thousand men, and all of them satisfied. Everyone had enough.

Restless isn't the word Luke uses, friend. Luke 9:17 says, "They all ate and were satisfied…" Every person ate and had enough. I know what a growling stomach feels like, and this verse is the opposite.

Seven basketfuls shows up in a different feeding story (Mark 8:8), so it's an easy one to mix up. In this passage, the disciples "…picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over." (Luke 9:17) Twelve is the number to hold on to here.
